title: Regiment and Bridge
premise: In 1899, Orsen Ravensworth drives for militant suffragist Edith Ravensworth—his aunt by blood, his employer by necessity—screening her correspondence and memorizing which letters to burn. When a six-year-old girl, the daughter of a hanged organizer, is left at their door with orders to forget her face, Orsen must smuggle her out of London as police close in and informers circle the household. The final berth on a departing emigrant ship can hold only one: the child, or Edith herself, now facing arrest. Orsen gives the berth to the child, stays behind to burn the archive that would condemn dozens, and is transported in Edith's place—but he leaves knowing the girl carries the movement's future across the water.
about_author: Rosalind Marchetti is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffrage-era letters in northern England before turning to fiction. She writes about the quiet people history forgot—the drivers, laundresses, and doorkeepers who made other people's courage possible.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. We learn his method: reading every letter, weighing each word like luggage, deciding what survives the fire. A coded note warns of an informant inside the household. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, and its first hairline crack when Orsen realizes he has begun caring whose secrets he burns.

chapters.title: The Face at the Door
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On a rain-slicked night, a child named Ida is left with a note: forget this face. She is the daughter of Thomas Wren, hanged for organizing mill workers—and she looks exactly like him. Police canvass the street within hours. Emotional beat: terror curdling into fierce protectiveness as Orsen breaks his own rule and keeps something instead of destroying it.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, with one interlude from Ida's. The informant is exposed; Edith is marked for arrest under new sedition statutes. A sympathetic shipping clerk offers one berth on the midnight steamer to Canada. Edith orders Orsen to take it himself. Emotional beat: rising dread and the unbearable arithmetic of love—who gets saved, and what saving costs.

chapters.title: Forget This Face
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He puts Ida on the ship with Edith's archive sewn into her coat, then returns to burn the rest and stand in Edith's place when the constables come. Years later, a letter arrives from Canada bearing a face he was told to forget. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into justice outside the law—Orsen loses everything except the knowledge that he chose rightly.
